title: Finite base change of strict localizations along a finite morphism
statement:
Let $h:T\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $S'=S_{(\bar s)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. For every connected component $i$ of the finite geometric fibre $T_{\bar s}=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product], take its unique geometric point with field $\Omega$ and write $\bar t_i:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ for the projection. The canonical map
$$\coprod_{i\in\pi_0(T_{\bar s})}T_{(\bar t_i)}\longrightarrow T\times_SS'$$
is an isomorphism over $T$ and $S'$. Each summand is a finite strictly henselian local $S'$-scheme: its coordinate ring is henselian local with separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and the induced extension of closed-point residue fields is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. The indexing set may be empty.

For any cartesian square $W=Y\times_ST$ with $Y\to S$ arbitrary, and any geometric point $\bar w:\operatorname{Spec}\Xi\to W$ with projections $\bar y$, $\bar t$ and common image $\bar u$ in $S$ (all using the same algebraically closed field $\Xi$), the maps of strict localizations induced by the projections [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] give a canonical isomorphism
$$W_{(\bar w)}\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_{(\bar y)}\times_{S_{(\bar u)}}T_{(\bar t)}.$$
This isomorphism commutes with the structural maps to $W$, $Y_{(\bar y)}$ and $T_{(\bar t)}$. No finiteness condition on $Y\to S$ is required.

source.place: Tag 05WR (lemma-quasi-finite-strict-henselization: finite local map and purely inseparable residue extension); Tag 0GIP (lemma-base-change-strict-henselization-quasi-finite), case (1), for the cartesian strict-localization square; finite-component decomposition in literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), proof, using algebra.tex Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian).

proof.text: By the strict-henselization functoriality theorem (1), S′=S_(s̄) is the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring whose closed point maps to s and whose residue field is κ(s̄), the separable algebraic closure of κ(s) inside Ω (in general a proper subfield of Ω, e.g. when Ω is transcendental over κ(s) or κ(s) is imperfect); s̄ factors through the closed point of S′, giving its canonical lift. For each geometric point t̄:Spec Ω→T with h t̄=s̄, part (3) of the same theorem supplies the unique local map T_(t̄)→S_(s̄) over h, and parts (1)–(2) give κ(s̄)⊂κ(t̄)⊂Ω.

source.place: Tag 04HX and the functoriality paragraph following Tag 03PS

proof.text: Choose an affine open Spec A⊂S containing s, with p⊂A the prime of s. Since h is finite, h^{-1}(Spec A)=Spec B′ with A→B′ finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and S′→S factors through Spec A, so by the affine fibre-product lemma T×_S S′=Spec B′×_{Spec A}Spec R=Spec B with R=O^sh_{S,s̄} and B=B′⊗_A R; by finite permanence (a) B is finite over R. R is henselian local, so the finite-over-henselian decomposition theorem gives B≅B_1×⋯×B_r with each B_i henselian local, finite over R, with R→B_i local and finite residue extension. Since B/m_RB is finite over the field κ(s̄), the primes of B over m_R are maximal; each lies in exactly one factor, so they are the maximal ideals n_1,…,n_r of the factors and B_i=B_{n_i}. Let q_i⊂B′ be the contraction of n_i. Because A→B′ is finite it is of finite type and quasi-finite at q_i (finite-ring-map lemma), so the quasi-finite strict-henselization lemma applies to (A→B′, p, q_i) for any compatible map κ(q_i)→Ω: B′^sh_{q_i} is the localization of A_p^sh⊗_{A_p}B′_{q_i}=R⊗_{A_p}B′_{q_i} at the prime given by that map to Ω, A_p^sh→B′^sh_{q_i} is finite local, and the residue extension is finite purely inseparable. As B′⊗_A R=B′_p⊗_{A_p}R and n_i contracts to q_i, the localization B_{n_i} equals (R⊗_{A_p}B′_{q_i})_{n_i}; so B_i≅B′^sh_{q_i}, the coordinate ring of T_(t̄_i), once n_i is matched with the prime determined by t̄_i (Step 3). The identification comes from the commutative diagram of the lemma, so its spectrum is the map with components j_T and the functorial map to S′ of Step 1.

source.place: Tags 04GH and 05WR; finite base change and finite-over-henselian factorization

proof.text: Matching of factors and components. T_s̄=Spec(B′⊗_AΩ) is finite over the algebraically closed field Ω, so it is a finite discrete space, each connected component is one point whose residue field is finite over Ω, hence equal to Ω; so each component has exactly one Ω-point over Ω, and its projection t̄_i is an S-morphism Spec Ω→T over s̄. Conversely every S-morphism Spec Ω→T over s̄ is a point of T_s̄ with residue field Ω (fibre-product universal property). Now B/m_RB=B′⊗_Aκ(s̄) and the residue field L_i of n_i is finite over the separably closed field κ(s̄); by the unique-embedding lemma L_i has exactly one embedding into Ω extending κ(s̄)⊂Ω, and composing B′→L_i→Ω gives an S-morphism t̄_i:Spec Ω→T over s̄ whose kernel on B′⊗_Aκ(s̄) is n_i. Conversely a t̄ over s̄ gives B′⊗_Aκ(s̄)→Ω (the separable closure κ(s̄) lies in Ω), whose kernel n is a prime over m_R, and t̄ is recovered from n by uniqueness of the embedding. So i↦n_i is a bijection π₀(T_s̄)→{primes of B over m_R}, and n_i is exactly the prime of R⊗_{A_p}B′_{q_i} determined by t̄_i in the quasi-finite lemma. If T_s̄ is empty, then B/m_RB=0, so B=0 by Nakayama (B finite over R) and both sides are empty. Hence the product map ∐_i T_(t̄_i)→T×_S S′ is an isomorphism over T and S′, and the finite-local and purely-inseparable residue assertions for each summand are those of the quasi-finite lemma; each summand's ring is strictly henselian by Step 1 applied to T.

source.place: Proposition Tag 03QP proof, using Algebra Tag 04GH; finite geometric fibre component decomposition

proof.text: Let W=Y×_ST, w̄:Spec Ξ→W with projections ȳ, t̄ and image ū∈S lying over u. Choose an affine open Spec A⊂S containing u and an affine open Spec C⊂Y over Spec A containing y; since h is finite, h^{-1}(Spec A)=Spec B with A→B finite. By the affine fibre-product lemma, W⊃Spec C×_{Spec A}Spec B=Spec(B⊗_AC), an open subscheme containing the image of w̄. Open immersions are ind-étale (each affine open is its own étale chart), so the ind-étale strict-local invariance lemma identifies W_(w̄), Y_(ȳ), T_(t̄), S_(ū) canonically, over W, Y, T, S, with the strict localizations of Spec(B⊗_AC), Spec C, Spec B, Spec A at the same geometric points, i.e. with the spectra of (B⊗_AC)_m^sh, C_r^sh, B_q^sh, A_p^sh formed by the pointed étale-neighbourhood construction; by uniqueness in functoriality (3) these identifications carry the functorial maps between the affine strict localizations to those between the strict localizations of S, Y, T, W. The tensor lemma for the finite map A→B and arbitrary A→C, with the point w̄ of Spec(B⊗_AC), gives B_q^sh⊗_{A_p^sh}C_r^sh≅(B⊗_AC)_m^sh induced by the structure maps; taking spectra and using the affine fibre-product lemma, Spec(B_q^sh⊗_{A_p^sh}C_r^sh)=T_(t̄)×_{S_(ū)}Y_(ȳ). Hence W_(w̄)≅Y_(ȳ)×_{S_(ū)}T_(t̄), with no hypothesis on Y→S beyond being a morphism of schemes.

source.place: Tag 0GIP, cases (1)/(4) (A→B finite), translated from affine rings to schemes via an affine open of W

proof.text: The tensor-product isomorphism is induced by the four canonical structure maps, so its composites with the projections and structural maps are the original functorial strict-localization maps. Uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property therefore gives commutation with W, Y_(ȳ) and T_(t̄), proving the stated compatibility.

lean.statement: theorem finite_strictLocalization_decomposition {T S : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ S) [IsFinite h] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) : Finite (ConnectedComponents (pullback h s : Scheme.{u})) ∧ Function.Bijective (fun t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s} ↦ ConnectedComponents.mk ((pullback.lift t.val (𝟙 _) (t.property.trans (Category.id_comp s).symm)) (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω))) ∧ ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (strictHenselizationRing s)), ∃ e : (∐ fun t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s} ↦ strictHenselizationScheme t.val) ≅ pullback h (strictHenselizationStructuralMap s), (∀ t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s}, Sigma.ι (fun t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s} ↦ strictHenselizationScheme t.val) t ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.fst h (strictHenselizationStructuralMap s) = strictHenselizationStructuralMap t.val) ∧ (∀ t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s}, Sigma.ι (fun t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s} ↦ strictHenselizationScheme t.val) t ≫ e.hom ≫ pullback.snd h (strictHenselizationStructuralMap s) = strictHenselizationMap h t.val ≫ eqToHom (congrArg strictHenselizationScheme t.property)) ∧ ∀ t : {t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ T // t ≫ h = s}, ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (strictHenselizationRing t.val)), IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing (strictHenselizationRing t.val) ∧ IsFinite (strictHenselizationMap h t.val ≫ eqToHom (congrArg strictHenselizationScheme t.property)) ∧ ∃ φ : strictHenselizationRing s →+* strictHenselizationRing t.val, Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) = strictHenselizationMap h t.val ≫ eqToHom (congrArg strictHenselizationScheme t.property) ∧ ∃ (_ : IsLocalHom φ), (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map φ).Finite ∧ @IsPurelyInseparable (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (strictHenselizationRing s)) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (strictHenselizationRing t.val)) _ _ (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map φ).toAlgebra
lean.note: The first theorem identifies the geometric lifts canonically with the connected components and gives the coproduct isomorphism and finite strictly henselian local factors, including their finite purely inseparable residue extensions. The second states the canonical strict-local square is a pullback for every original cartesian square; this is equivalent to the second canonical isomorphism with its structural-map compatibilities.
